title: problem of allocation and release memory. uC ARM M4 ATSAM4e8e
author: SIEMELBE

comments.body:
I found why "cJSON_Parse ()" does everything crash.
I am completely stupid.

in the function "fct_json_parse_login ()", to copy the character string, I directly incrude the pointer of the cjson structure (ptr_login_json, and ptr_pxd_json).

big error, suddenly when the json tree was destroyed, "cJSON_Delete ()" no longer understands anything.
it is I who breaks everything.

I don't understand your last comment.

But what I can see: There is only one place where memory is allocated: `cJSON_Parse`. Every other `cJSON*` is just an *alias*, but doesn't **own** the memory.  This means that to free the memory, all you have to do is `cJSON_Delete(root)`. Every other call to `cJSON_Delete` or `cJSON_free` would result in a double free, which can crash or even worse.

sorry for the time I took you.

my problem was, that to recover the characters of a string I incremented the pointer of the structure cjson ("valuestring"). I broke the whole structure.
sometimes stupidity has no limit.

I used "cjson_free ()" and "cjson_delete ()" to find a solution. but I understood that you should use "cjson_delete ()" only once.

the corrections are made, and it works very well.

Good day to you
Just use `strncpy` or `memcpy` if you know the length, they are there for a reason.

satisfaction_conditions: Understanding of proper memory management with cJSON library
Explanation of how cJSON memory ownership works
Guidance on proper string handling without corrupting JSON structures
A solution that prevents memory leaks in long-running embedded systems
Proper techniques for copying string data from JSON objects

_classification.category: Can be dockerized without any issue

dockerfile:
FROM ubuntu:20.04

# Avoid interactive prompts during package installation
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    && apt-get clean \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Create working directory
WORKDIR /app

# Clone the repository and checkout the specific commit that addresses the issue
RUN git clone https://github.com/DaveGamble/cJSON.git . \
    && git checkout c083421f408f0ee5012dca431baefe8791858a33

# Create build directory and build the project using CMake
RUN mkdir build \
    && cd build \
    && cmake .. \
    && make

# Since the issue is related to memory allocation and release on an ARM M4 microcontroller,
# this Dockerfile can only build the library. Testing the specific issue would require 
# additional embedded toolchains and hardware-specific setup.
CMD ["ls", "-la", "/app/build"]
